flashcard_questions.q: What does Fleance's torch symbolise at the opening of Act 2?
flashcard_questions.a: Truth and hope for the future.

flashcard_questions.q: Which line from Banquo shows that heaven has put out its lights?
flashcard_questions.a: “There's husbandry in heaven; / Their candles are all out.”

flashcard_questions.q: What disturbs Banquo's sleep in Act 2, Scene 1?
What is meant by a soliloquy in a play?
flashcard_questions.a: A speech by a character alone on stage, revealing their inner thoughts.

flashcard_questions.q: Which lines open Macbeth's dagger soliloquy?
flashcard_questions.a: “Is this a dagger which I see before me, / The handle toward my hand?”

flashcard_questions.q: Which phrase shows Macbeth suspecting the dagger is only a hallucination?
flashcard_questions.a: “A dagger of the mind, a false creation”

flashcard_questions.q: Why does Macbeth's line “There's no such thing” matter?
flashcard_questions.a: It confirms he is sane, so the murder is a conscious choice.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the blood on the dagger's “blade and dudgeon” foreshadow?
flashcard_questions.a: The guilt that will later consume both Macbeth and his wife.

flashcard_questions.q: Which goddess of witchcraft does Macbeth name in the soliloquy?
What does the word “knell” mean in Macbeth's closing rhyming couplet?
flashcard_questions.a: A funeral bell — he is pronouncing Duncan's death sentence.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does Shakespeare keep Duncan's murder offstage?
flashcard_questions.a: Regicide was thought too sinful to depict, and an imagined act hits harder.

flashcard_questions.q: Which monosyllabic line does Macbeth speak on returning from the murder?
Which rebuke does Lady Macbeth give when Macbeth will not return the daggers?
flashcard_questions.a: “Infirm of purpose! / Give me the daggers.”

flashcard_questions.q: Which word stuck in Macbeth's throat as he heard the grooms pray?
Which voice does Macbeth hear immediately after killing Duncan?
flashcard_questions.a: “Sleep no more! / Macbeth does murder sleep.”

notes: 15 cards: 8 character or theme to quotation, 4 quotation-to-effect (torch, dudgeon, knell, 'no such thing'), 1 term-to-definition (soliloquy), 1 allusion card (Hecate), 1 staging card (the offstage murder). Dropped Tarquin so that only one allusion card competes with Hecate, and dropped 'symbolically', 'dramatic irony', 'allusions' and 'rhyming couplet' as definition cards — each is already tested through a named example in the scene.
